viewer_sees: Zeus standing over the beaten Titan on the scorched war plain, the thunderbolt blazing in his raised fist; Cronus brought down on his knees, his great head bowed below the god's
Zeus and a new wife side by side on the marble terrace of Olympus; a vast cold shadow in the shape of the old Titan slides across the marble behind them and Zeus turns his head toward it
Metis alone, sea-grey and calm, a knowing half-smile; in her hand the same drained bronze kylix Zeus held in Part 1

Zeus small on a bare peak at night; the mountain range behind him is the reclining body of a giant woman and the starry sky above bends down as a giant man of stars, both great faces leaning in to speak
storm cloud folding into a helmeted young woman with a spear, exactly as tall as Zeus, face to face with him at eye level across the terrace
a crowned youth of black storm cloud rising behind the summit, taller than the mountain, towering over the empty throne of Olympus; Zeus far below looking up, the thunderbolt in his hand dimming
Zeus leaning close with his mouth at Metis's ear, an arm around her; she turns toward him, and her whole form loosens into a stream of sea-blue light drawn into his open mouth
callback to Part 1 — Cronus in his torchlit basalt hall, head tipped back, the swaddled stone lifted to his mouth
PROCESS CUTAWAY — Zeus's torso opened like a chamber, the way Part 1 opened Cronus; Metis curled inside in sea-blue dark, and inside her one small golden light already burning
Zeus on his throne clutching his head with both hands, white-gold light gathering behind his brow and leaking through his fingers, the sky over Olympus cracking with thunder
a bronze double axe at the top of its swing against a storm sky, lightning running along its edge; no one holding it is seen
Athena bursting up out of a blaze of white-gold light, fully grown, in golden armour, spear shaken high and mouth open in a war cry; Zeus behind her on the throne, hand still at his head
the whole summit of Olympus shaking, snow avalanching down its slopes, the Aegean heaving in dark swells below, and high in the sky the sun god reining his four fire horses to a stop
Athena portrait — helmet pushed back off her face, grey eyes level; a spear grounded in one hand and a spindle of spun wool in the other, war and craft in one figure
Zeus enthroned at night with his head tilted as if listening; a soft sea-blue glow in his chest, and in it the faint shape of a seated woman leaning up toward his heart
Athena and Poseidon facing each other across the bare rock of the Acropolis, the small early town and the plain of Attica below them
Poseidon drives the trident into the rock and a spring of salt water bursts up; beside it, where Athena kneels, an olive sapling pushes up out of the stone and spreads silver leaves
Poseidon colossal out in the bay, the trident raised, a long wall of sea rolling in over the plain; the rock of the Acropolis with its one olive tree standing dry above the flood
Athena turning a bronze key in a sealed bronze door deep in Olympus; the door opens a hand's width and white-gold thunderbolt light floods out over her

Hera on the terrace turning her back on the bright throne hall where Zeus and his armoured daughter sit, and looking down through a break in the cloud at one small pregnant woman on the earth far below
Leto, heavily pregnant, hurrying along a rocky coast with her mantle tearing in the wind; above her Hera vast in a bank of storm cloud, her shadow sweeping over the land after her
ANIMATED MAP — the Aegean on bronze; a thin line of light drawn from land to land, and every coast and island it touches goes dark and turns away, until the line runs out toward one unmarked speck
Delos drifting loose on open sea — a small bare rock seen from just above the waterline, its jagged underside showing as the swell lifts it; Leto a small figure climbing onto its shore
Leto kneeling on the bare rock with her palm flat on the stone, while the whole island shudders and sheds rocks into the waves around it
Leto standing with one hand raised to swear; behind her, over the bare rock, a mirage of a white marble temple heaped with gold offerings shimmers up out of the air
TIMELINE — Delos in one locked view, Leto lying under a single palm tree while sun and moon race across the sky over and over, nine days and nine nights

Hera seated on Olympus with a young torch-bearing goddess at her feet, Hera's hand resting on her shoulder, the girl unaware; far below through the clouds, a tiny island ringed with gathered goddesses
the rainbow messenger flying low over the sea with wings of rainbow light, an immense golden necklace streaming behind her in long loops
Leto on her knees with both arms around the trunk of the palm; the ground under her ripples with sudden flowers and light, and a burst of golden light breaks out at her knees
the newborn god radiant in white cloth in the grass under the palm, and gold spreading out from him across the rocks, flowers and shore of the island until all of Delos is gold
Apollo portrait — the young god standing on golden Delos, a lyre in one arm and a bow across his back, speaking out over the sea
a small girl kneeling beside her mother under the palm, steadying her with both hands and looking toward the light where her twin is coming
Artemis portrait in motion — running through a mountain forest with her bow, a deer bounding at her side
Leto alone in the rain before a shut city gate, seen from behind, the gate towers dark above her
a mortal woman in labour in a lamplit room at night, praying toward the open window; through it, a silver figure with a bow standing on the moonlit hill
Apollo at the foot of the Parnassus cliffs loosing an arrow into a huge coiling serpent by the spring; the arrow strikes and the serpent writhes
TIMELINE — Delphi in one locked view down the mountainside; the temple rises and treasuries multiply while envoys with offerings climb the sacred way, and the seasons cycle over the cliffs
the same grey stone from Part 1 on a stone base at Delphi, glistening with oil, a skein of unspun wool laid across it
Apollo standing in his temple with one hand resting on the stone, light falling between the columns behind him
historical Delos — Athenian warships in the sacred harbour and a herald on the temple steps reading out a decree to a crowd
a small boat rowing a pregnant woman away from Delos at dusk; on the shore behind, beside the temple, the lone sacred palm
Athena, Apollo and Artemis seen from behind on a high ledge of Olympus at dawn, three figures looking out over the world
Athena on Olympus with the bronze key hanging at her belt, the thunderbolt chamber open behind her, its white-gold light on her shoulders
Artemis with her bow and Apollo with his lyre standing together on the golden shore of Delos, the drifting island fixed and shining behind them
EMPTY AFTERMATH — beside Zeus's throne on Olympus, a second throne that no one has ever sat in, a crown resting on its empty seat, cloud drifting across it
Zeus close, eyes closed, and a faint sea-blue glow still alive inside his chest

two kings mirrored across one frame — Cronus on his throne in the basalt hall with the swaddled stone, Zeus on his throne on Olympus with the sea-blue glow in his chest — the same pose, a generation apart
teaser for Part 4: a net of fine golden links, almost invisible, drawn tight over a bed in red forge light
MACRO OBJECT — an olive branch, a golden lyre and a silver bow side by side on one stone ledge

END CARD — Athena, Apollo and Artemis squared to camera across the frame, each with the scenes of their birth small behind them and their symbol at the lower edge, open space for the title and the SUBSCRIBE button
